devices.note: Every polygon of the shipped DXF; Dinh Fig. 2B's four panels at the positions their traces registered (each panel's own 50 µm bar read with its anti-aliased ends).  Dinh prints no whole-device drawing at a known scale (Fig. 2A's main panel read at the 3.2 mm width gives 60.6 mm against the printed 75.8 mm), so there is no underlay; the device's length against the printed 75.8 mm is the conditional conflict of PRESET_PROVENANCE.

devices.title: Gifford 2014 Fig. 4 bead device (design level), opencif rc6

panels.title: Gifford Fig. 4 inset, the end of leg 4

devices.note: Gifford's Fig. 4 schematic is not drawn to scale (p. 4502), so there is no underlay; the inset (leg 4's end) is placed where its trace registered.  The preset takes the inset's leg spacing (818 µm, rc6), so the neighbouring leg 2 in the inset lies where the image shows it by construction (consistency, not a test): its posts and centre line on the image's, its side walls wider on the image (recorded, not claimed; rc6_traces README).

devices.name: gifford2014_fig6_design
devices.title: Gifford 2014 Fig. 6 platelet device (design level, the micrograph's leg axes), opencif rc6

panels.title: Gifford Fig. 6 micrograph, one map for the four legs and their turns

devices.note: Gifford's Fig. 6 schematic is topology only (not to scale), so there is no underlay; the micrograph (the ends of legs 7, 5, 3, 1 and the turns of 5, 3, 1) is placed where its one-map trace registered it.  The preset takes the micrograph's layout (rc6): legs 1, 3, 5, 7 on its rows, legs 2, 4, 6 where semicircular turns about the turn walls' common centre (1745.7 µm beyond leg 1) put them -- only 8-23 degrees of each turn are in the frame, so legs 2, 4, 6 are an assumption; leg 7's array ends 4 rows beyond the image's (LIMITATIONS 25).
